title: Group Anagrams
statement: A word-puzzle app wants to bundle its answer bank so that scrambled variants of the same letters live together. Given a list of lowercase strings words, return a list of groups (each a list of strings) where every group contains exactly the words that are anagrams of one another: two words are anagrams when one is a rearrangement of the other's letters, using every letter exactly as many times as it occurs. Duplicated input words each appear in their group once per occurrence. Within a group, words must keep their original input order; groups must be ordered by the position in words where each group's first member appears. If words is empty, return an empty list.
hints: Two anagrams differ only in letter order. Can you compute one canonical value that is identical for every rearrangement of the same letters, and bucket words by it?

Use a dict mapping a derived key to the list of words seen so far with that key. The key must capture letter multiplicities, not just which letters occur, and it must be hashable: sorted(w) is a list (unhashable), and set(w) drops counts, so ''.join(sorted(w)) or a tuple of 26 letter counts is the right key.

Scan words once; for each w compute key = ''.join(sorted(w)) and do groups.setdefault(key, []).append(w). Because Python dicts preserve insertion order, list(groups.values()) already yields groups ordered by first appearance, with each group's words in input order.
